en: Mahāmantrānusāriṇī. C.0.1. Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Mahāmantrānusāriṇī!
Homage to the King of Vidyās!
Homage to all Buddhas!

C.1.1.a. Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha, in the Bamboo Grove, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. C.1.1.b. Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vaiśālī.
At the hall of the peaked-roofed pavilion on the bank of the Markaṭahrada lake,
the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:
"Come, Ānanda, let us go to Vaiśālī."
"So be it, Venerable Sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, wandering on a tour through the Vṛji country, arrived at Vaiśālī and stayed there in the Āmrapālī grove.
There, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda.

Go, Ānanda! Having gone to Vaiśālī, place your foot upon the Indra-pillar and recite these mantra-words following the Great Mantra, as well as these verses: C.2.1. Visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata!
C.2.2. The Buddha, who has compassion for the world, commands:
by the authorization of all Buddhas, and by the authorization of all Pratyekabuddhas.
With the approval of all Arhats (or, according to the AFGH manuscript:
with the approval of all beings), and with the approval of all those in training.
With the approval of all śrāvakas; with the approval of all truthful speech; with the approval of the pratyekabuddhas and Brahmās.
With the approval of Brahmā;
with the approval of Kāmeśvara; with the approval of Indra.
With the approval of the gods; with the approval of the lords of the asuras;
with the approval of all the asuras.
By the command of the messengers of the Asuras;
by the consent of all beings.
C.2.3. Spread forth! Spread forth! Spread forth! Spread forth! Spread forth!
C.2.4. The Buddha, who has compassion for the world, commands:
"Release! Release! Release! Release!
Do not remain!"
May the plague be pacified!
Go forth, go forth, go forth!

Buddha enters—the Great God, the God beyond gods, the Teacher of gods; and the gods together with Indra, together with Brahmā, together with Prajāpati, and the four World-Protectors enter, along with many others.
Thousands of deities and lords of the asuras,
many thousands of asuras,
and many thousands of spirits who are devoted to the Blessed One will enter there for the sake of all sentient beings.
C.2.6. They will bring you misfortune. Go forth! Go forth! Go forth! Go forth!
Cast off [this state] and flee!
If you are of evil intent, do not flee, for you shall perish!
But those who possess a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*), who desire not to commit offenses, and who wish to follow the protection—let them remain and enter the assembly.
Thus does the Buddha, who has compassion for the world, command.
C.2.8. *Sumuru* 4, *suru* 4, *huru* 4, *mu* 4—he enters.

*Muru* 8, *miri* 6, *muru miri* 13, *muru mirīti* 6, *ri* 6, *rī* 6, *miri* 6, *tiri hasa miri ti mirī ri miri*. The agent (*kartā*), the action (*karaṃ*), the agent (*kartā*), the small stones (*kaṃkarā*), the saws (*karakacā*). The small stones (*kaṃkarā*) 8; the small stone (*kaṃkara*) and the wandering one (*caṅkari*) in the *kurīśe* [region].
Kaṃkari 3 ṣeti / Ri 6 rephasāri / Phuri 7 pharā anāthānāthā siri thi phuri ruri prāsturi anāthānāthā nirgacchata ripūṃ nirgacchata! If you, with evil minds, do not flee, you shall perish.
C.2.9. The Buddha, who has compassion for the world, thus commands:
He enters with a resolute intention for the welfare of all sentient beings, abiding in loving-kindness, compassionate, abiding in sympathetic joy, and abiding in equanimity.
C.2.10. These mantra-words are perfected; they are the perfected verses spoken by the Victor.
For it is for the benefit of all the deities and those beings who desire our welfare.
Through supreme wisdom today, and likewise through the nature of reality (dharmatā), may all the plagues of the worlds be pacified; may you possess good health.
C.3.1. He whose craving has been shattered and thinned out, whose mind is peaceful and free from exertion—he shall bring you well-being.
CDFGH: Throughout: *sarvaḥ svasti* (C.3.2). He who is the leader who establishes the world upon the path to liberation;
The teacher of all dharmas—he shall bring you well-being.
C.3.3. He who is the refuge, the teacher of the world, by whom much happiness has been brought about for the sake of all sentient beings—he shall bring you well-being.
C.3.4. May that Protector, by whom this entire world has been constantly protected with a mind of loving-kindness like a son, grant you well-being.
C.3.5. He who is the refuge, the protection, the island, and the ultimate resort for all sentient beings wandering in saṃsāra—he shall bring you well-being.
C.3.6. He who is directly non-deceptive regarding all phenomena, who is pure, whose speech is pure, and who brings about purity—may he grant you well-being.
C.3.7. He, the great hero, at whose birth all prosperities flourished—he who has accomplished his purpose and perfected his equipment—shall bring you well-being.
He, at whose birth this earth with its treasures trembled,
and by whom all sentient beings were filled with joy— he shall bring you well-being.
He, at whose awakening the earth shook with its six kinds of transformations and Māra became dejected, will bring you well-being.
May he whose fame was established when the Wheel of Dharma was set in motion by the Sage as he proclaimed the Noble Truths— may he grant you well-being.
He by whom all the Tīrthakaras were conquered through the Dharma by the Protector (Tāyin),
and who has brought all the assemblies under his control— he shall bring you well-being.
C.3.12. May the Buddha grant you well-being; may the gods, together with Śakra, grant you well-being;
may all beings grant you well-being at all times.

C.3.13. By the power of the Buddha’s merit and by the approval of the deities, may whatever purpose is intended be fully accomplished today. C.3.14. May there be well-being for you bipeds; may there be well-being for you quadrupeds.
May there be well-being for you as you travel on the road, and well-being when you have returned.
May there be well-being at night, may there be well-being by day, and may there be well-being when midday has arrived;
may there be well-being for you everywhere, and may no evil come upon them.
C.3.16. May all beings, all living creatures, and all spirits without exception—may they all indeed be happy; may they all be free from illness;
may they all behold auspicious things; and may no one encounter evil.

C.3.17. Whatever beings have gathered here, whether stationed on the earth or in the atmosphere, let them always maintain loving-kindness toward all creatures, and let them practice the Dharma by day and by night.

C.4. "So be it, Venerable Sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Placing his foot upon the threshold pillar, he spoke these mantra-words following the Great Mantra, as well as these verses:
C.5.1. *Visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata!* (Depart, depart, depart, depart, depart!)
C.5.2. The Buddha, who has compassion for the world, commands:
by the consent of all Buddhas, and by the consent of all Pratyekabuddhas.
With the approval of all Arhats;
with the approval of all those in training; with the approval of all Śrāvakas.
By the approval of all truthful speech;
by the approval of each Brahmā;
by the approval of Brahmā.
By the permission of Kāmeśvara; by the permission of Indra;
by the permission of the gods.
With the approval of the lord of the asuras;
with the approval of all the asuras; with the approval of the servants of the asuras.
With the consent of all beings:
go forth, go forth, go forth, go forth, go forth!
The Buddha, who has compassion for the world, commands.
Release, release, release, release!
Let them not remain!
May the calamity be pacified!
Depart! Depart! Depart! Depart!
Buddha enters—the Great God, the God beyond gods, the Teacher of gods; and the gods together with Indra, together with Brahmā, together with Prajāpati, and the four world-protectors enter;
as do many thousands of deities and the lords of the asuras.
Many thousands of asuras will enter,
and many thousands of spirits, having gained faith in the Blessed One, will enter for the sake of all sentient beings;
they will bring about your welfare.
Go forth! Go forth! Go forth! Go forth!
Flee quickly!
If you do not flee with evil intent, you shall perish.
Those who possess minds of loving-kindness, who do not desire to commit offenses, and who wish to maintain protection—let them remain and enter into my thought.
Thus does the Buddha, out of compassion for the world, command:
*sumuru 4 suru 4 huru 4 mu 4 praviśati*.
Muru 8 miri 6 muru miri 13 muru mirīti 6 ri 6 rī 6 miri 6 tiri hasa miri ti mirī ri miri kartā karaṃ kartā kaṃkarā karakacā / kaṃkarā 8 kaṃkaro caṃkariti kurīśe / kaṃkari 3 ṣeti /

Ri 6: Rephasāri! Phuri 7: O you who are without a protector, the glorious one has appeared; o you who are without a protector, depart, depart from Ruri Prāsturi! Depart from the enemies, depart! If you are of evil mind, do not flee, do not perish! Thus does the Buddha, the compassionate one for the world, command.
He enters with the resolute intention for the welfare of all sentient beings, dwelling in loving-kindness, compassionate, dwelling in sympathetic joy, and dwelling in equanimity.
These mantra-words are perfected, these perfected verses spoken by the Victors,
belonging indeed to all the deities and spirits who desire the welfare [of others].
Through supreme wisdom today, and likewise through the nature of reality (dharmatā), may all the plagues of the worlds be pacified; may you possess health.
He whose craving has been severed, shattered, and thinned out,
whose mind is peaceful and free from exertion— he shall bring you well-being.
C.6.2. That Leader who establishes the world upon the path to liberation, the teacher of all dharmas—he shall bring you well-being.
C.6.3. May he who is the refuge, the teacher of the world, by whom much happiness has been brought about for the sake of all sentient beings—he shall bring you well-being.
May he, the Protector, by whom this entire world has always been guarded with a mind of loving-kindness like a son, grant you well-being.
He who is the refuge, the protection, the island, and the ultimate resort for all sentient beings wandering in saṃsāra— he shall bring you well-being.
He who is the direct non-deceiver of all phenomena, pure,
whose speech is pure, and who brings about purity— he shall bring you well-being.
C.6.7. He, the great hero, at whose birth all prosperities were fulfilled—the one whose purpose was accomplished and whose equipment was perfected—he shall bring you well-being.
He, at whose birth this earth, rich in treasures, was shaken,
and by whom all sentient beings were filled with joy— he shall bring you well-being.
He under whose awakening the earth shook with its sixfold movement and Māra was despondent— he shall bring you well-being.
C.6.10. May he whose fame was established when the Wheel of Dharma was set in motion, as he proclaimed the Noble Truths—he shall bring you well-being.
He by whom all the Tīrthakaras have been conquered through the Dharma, the Protector, who has brought all the hosts under his control— he shall bring you well-being.
C.6.12. May the Buddha grant you well-being; may the gods, together with Śakra, grant you well-being;
may all beings grant you well-being at all times.

C.6.13. By the power of the Buddha’s merit and by the approval of the deities, may whatever purpose is intended be fulfilled today in its entirety. C.6.14. May there be well-being for you bipeds; may there be well-being for you quadrupeds.
May there be well-being for you as you travel on the road, and may there be well-being when you have returned.
May there be well-being at night, well-being by day, and well-being when midday has arrived;
may there be well-being for you everywhere, and may no evil come upon them.
C.3.16. May all beings, all living creatures, and all spirits without exception—may they all indeed be happy; may they all be free from illness;
may they all behold auspicious things; and may no one encounter evil.

C.3.17. Whatever beings have gathered here, whether dwelling on the earth or in the atmosphere, let them always practice loving-kindness toward all creatures and walk in the Dharma by day and by night.
C.7.1. Thus, there, through the power of the Buddhas and the power of the deities, that great calamity was pacified.
C.7.2. The Blessed One said this, and the monks, those bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
C.8. (A) The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra Entitled "The Great Protective Spell Following the Mantras" is completed.
(B) The Noble Great Protective Spell Following the Mantras is completed.
(C) Thus, the Following of the Mantras is fully concluded.
(E) Thus concludes the Noble Great Queen of Spells, the Great Knowledge that Follows the Mantras.

(F) Thus concludes the Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled *The Great Protection: Following the Great Mantras*, including the Ritual for Protection. May there be auspiciousness for all the world! C.9. (A) May there be well-being for the entire universe!
Of those phenomena that arise from a cause, the Tathāgata has declared their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa. May there be auspiciousness!
